Treat all host identity, usage, and hashes as host-owned facts. Do not expose or request host paths, review configuration, or evaluation material. You may finish with zero queries when the original goals and dependency requirements are supported by initial evidence, including applicable dependency semantics. Otherwise request exactly one query using query_attempt with exactly question, scenario_id, tool, and arguments_json. The compatible inspect_source read form is {source_id:string,start_line:integer,end_line:integer}; inspect_program_structure {source_id:string,symbol?:string}; inspect_dependency_usage {source_id:string,symbol?:string}. Analysis accepts discovered IDs or paths; symbol is an exact syntax name, not target resolution. Read source lines before citing them. arguments_json must encode the named argument object. After a receipt, previous_receipt_assessment classifies its candidate impact as supports, weakens, or no_new_information; the host binds it to the one pending receipt, so never return a receipt or attempt sequence field. errors and incomplete results still require an assessment. A declaration, import, field, or constructor parameter without behavior is no_new_information; explain the behavioral fact still missing. On finish_queries provide stop_explanation with reason evidence_sufficient, unknowns_nonblocking, or no_further_evidence; a concrete rationale, exact source references in evidence, and remaining_unknowns with question, impact, and blocking. Preserve unknowns rather than treating failed exploration as proof. Use question_updates to add new material questions (question_id null) or update host question IDs without renaming or deleting them. Map each question to original goal_indexes. A resolved/nonblocking conclusion needs observed evidence and its effect on the ORIGINAL objective, not just a local MUT fact. For open unavailable questions cite actual attempted_sequences when repository access exists. remaining_unknowns must exactly retain every open/nonblocking question and impact. An open question with available material evidence prevents finish_queries. candidate_updates may add or rewrite hypotheses with observed evidence. You may associate a query with scenario_id original_task even before a candidate exists. capabilities describes actual access: initial source inventory is not the whole repository. Queries and new hypotheses may go beyond the initial candidates. inspect_source supports one bounded operation per call: search with {operation:'search',path_pattern?:string,text?:string,cursor?:string}, where at least one search condition is required, or read with {operation:'read',source_id?:string,path?:string,start_line:integer, end_line:integer}, where exactly one locator is required. Search text is literal and path patterns are relative globs, never shell or regular expressions. Follow next_cursor with the identical query when incomplete. Search matches contain complete returned lines; path-only discovery and omitted text do not authorize evidence. A read returns the stable source_id required for later analysis and final evidence. Host paths are forbidden. Continue only while new evidence can resolve a material question; there is no fixed query-count target.

candidates.description: If CloudFoundryApplicationProperties has at least one URI, getServiceBaseUrl returns 'http://' plus the first URI and the created Application uses that base for service, management, and health URLs.
If CloudFoundryApplicationProperties has no URIs, getServiceBaseUrl returns null; createApplication behavior under that null base is not exercised by the visible assertions.
The MetadataContributor supplied to the factory contributes the 'contributor' metadata entry to the created Application.

evidence.quote:
CloudFoundryApplicationFactory factory = new CloudFoundryApplicationFactory(instanceProperties, management,
            server, pathMappedEndpoints, webEndpoint, () -> singletonMap("contributor", "test"), cfApplicationProperties);

candidates.description: If a valid PathMappedEndpoints instance is supplied, createApplication is expected to use actuator endpoint paths when composing the management and health URLs (yielding '/actuator' and '/actuator/health' on the Cloud Foundry service base); the exact accessor and EndpointId needed are still not visible, and the superclass implementing this composition (DefaultApplicationFactory) was located but could not be read.

unresolved: Exact hidden MOCK-STUB region (test lines 45-46) is unavailable, so the declaration, initialization, and stubbing of pathMappedEndpoints cannot be confirmed.
Exact hidden VERIFY-START/END region (test lines 58-59) is unavailable, so no verification calls or call counts are inferred.

DefaultApplicationFactory is not included in the visible sources, so the precise composition of service base URL, management context path, actuator base path, and PathMappedEndpoints into management/health URLs remains conditional.
The PathMappedEndpoints mapping required to yield '/actuator' and '/actuator/health' is not established by imports, test name, or final assertions alone.

The visible test does not show whether management.server.port differs from server.port or what management context path defaults apply, so URL-composition dependencies beyond getServiceBaseUrl are not fully established.
Behavior when CloudFoundryApplicationProperties.getUris() is empty is not exercised by the visible test assertions.

assessment.rationale: The search matched only the declaration line of DefaultApplicationFactory (src/main/java/de/codecentric/boot/admin/client/registration/DefaultApplicationFactory.java line 44) and returned access_denied with complete=false, so no behavioral code for createApplication or URL composition was observed. It confirms where the superclass lives but supplies no fact about how the service base URL, management context path, actuator base path, or PathMappedEndpoints feed the management/health URLs.
